## Step 3 — the first member is verified end to end

GoogleCalendarEventCreator is now running the queue's **full** mechanism, agentic lane included. Three defects had to land first, all found by the flip's own traffic rather than by rehearsal:

| | found by | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| #906 | a member's mount vs canon's tree | #907 — `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set |
| #922 | following the park's own re-queue instruction | #925 — letting go of an open item kills your claim |
| #921 | following DESIGN §8's force recipe | open — §8 says to strip `task:blocked` without adding `task:ready`, which yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick |

### Evidence

- **B1 on a member** — 02:00Z, the tick instantiated 15 standing items (GCEC #904–#918); the last slot-era item was #903 at 00:09Z.
- **B7, on real traffic and not as planned** — the fault was the missing **endpoint declaration**, not the unset secret. `taskScheduler.endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet: this one. Six items parked `needs-human` naming the fault, no session started (GCEC #908 et al).
- **B3 on a member** — GCEC #908 `grow_with_claudinite/growth-dedup`: claim → hand-off with nonce → live session at 11:16:12Z → `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z, its work landed as GCEC #923. First live agentic run on a flipped member.
- **#922's fix confirmed live** — GCEC #909 re-queued at 11:47:53Z and claimed *and won* at 11:48:06Z. Before the fix that same sequence lost the arbitration to the parked episode's claim and dropped the item.
- All five remaining parked items re-queued and draining: #909, #911 executing; #913, #915, #918 ready.

### What this says about the burst

Step 2 was thorough and every one of these three still got past it, for one reason each: canon runs the engine from its repo root rather than a mount (#906); the simulator modelled F18's *intent* rather than its artifact, so it was correct by construction and blind (#922); and no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes (#921). The burst proved the mechanism. What it could not prove was the mechanism *as a member receives it*.

### Remaining before the slot deletion

- [ ] **12 more members need a CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN`** — #916, owner-only, one checkbox per repo. Every adopted member is affected: all of them declare `basics` + `tidy-repo` + `grow_with_claudinite`, which carry 8 agentic tasks between them.
- [ ] The per-member mini-burst for each, once wired — GCEC is the worked example and took three canon fixes; the rest should take none.
- [ ] #921 folded in (small).
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR.

#924 is split out as latent and not blocking: a losing claimant's own comment bumps `updated_at`, so contention postpones the leash reclaim it depends on. #925 removes the common source of those losing claims; the property survives it.

{"number":922,"title":"A needs-human park leaves its claim standing, so the item livelocks forever once re-queued","body":"Caught on live traffic doing exactly what the engine's own message instructs. #801 Step 3, B7's second half.

## The throwing call site

[`queue/executor.mjs:92-99`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L92) — `claimWinner`:

```js
const boundary = sorted.filter((c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(EPISODE_MARKER)).at(-1);
const claims = sorted
  .filter((c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(CLAIM_MARKER))
  .filter((c) => !boundary || c.id > boundary.id);
return claims[0] ?? null;
```

With no `EPISODE_MARKER` anywhere on the item, `boundary` is `undefined`, the filter is a no-op, and `claims[0]` is the **oldest claim the item ever received**. Every later executor claims the item, reads back a claim that is not its own, logs `another executor holds this episode's earliest claim — moving on`, and drops it — leaving the item `task:executing` with nobody executing. The tick's executing-leash reclaim returns it to `task:ready` ~1h later and the cycle repeats. Forever.

The comment block immediately above that function names this exact hazard and states the invariant it depends on:

> Over an item's lifetime dead claims accumulate … arbitrating over all of them makes a dead claim outrank every future live claimant — the item then livelocks through reclaim cycles forever. **The reclaim / revert / re-queue comment is the boundary.**

## Which side fails to hold it up

Three paths post the marker — the tick's reclaim ([`tick.mjs:230`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs#L230)), the F15 revert ([`executor.mjs:174`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L174)), and the hand-wake ([`create-work-item.mjs:64`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/create-work-item.mjs#L64)).

The **`needs-human` park does not**. It posts a plain comment and stops ([`executor.mjs:326`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L326)) — and that comment is the *instruction to re-queue*:

> No session was started. Fix the invocation endpoint, then re-queue this item (remove `needs-human`, add `task:ready`).

Follow it exactly and you get a permanently unclaimable item. The engine tells you to do the thing that breaks it.

## Observed

GoogleCalendarEventCreator #908 (`grow_with_claudinite/growth-dedup`):

| | |
|---|---|
| 04:55:30Z | claimed by `actions-31927761001` |
| 04:55:53Z | parked `needs-human` — no endpoint configured. **Claim comment left standing** |
| 11:14:12Z | re-queued per the printed instruction: `needs-human` off, `task:ready` on |
| 11:14:26Z | claimed by `actions-31943780210` |
| 11:14:27Z | [same run](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/actions/runs/31943780210) loses to the 04:55 claim and moves on — it lost the race to itself |

Unblocked by hand by posting the marker and re-readying.

## Fix

The `needs-human` park is a terminal convergence of the episode, so it belongs in the same class as reclaim and revert: post `EPISODE_MARKER` when parking. Then the printed instruction stays true as written and no operator has to know the marker exists.

Worth checking the other terminal paths for the same omission, and pinning it with a test that re-queues a parked item and asserts the next claim wins — a single-claim test cannot see this, which is why the whole burst missed it (the `basics/writing-tests` rule about calling a helper twice across a re-queue is exactly this shape).

Ties into #892: both are terminal-convergence side effects that a session or a park is trusted to perform and doesn't.

input.body:
The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [x] The first member flipped, wired and observed end to end — agentless and agentic
- [ ] All members flipped and observed; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] Step 4: the fielded engine matches DESIGN §15.14–24 — #883 closed
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

Since this repo flipped to the work-item queue, every **agentic** work item has parked `needs-human`: `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*, before it ever looks for a token, because no `taskScheduler.endpoints` was declared. The agentless lane was unaffected throughout.

`endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet (the canon), so this affected every member. GoogleCalendarEventCreator was wired first as the worked example and has since run a real agentic item end to end.

## The change

- `.claudinite-checks.json` gains `taskScheduler.endpoints.default` — this repo's routine URL, and `tokenSecret: "CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN"` (already set on this repo).
- Both workflow files gain `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` under the `# claudinite:secrets` marker.

The workflow halves are **generated, not hand-written**: the output of running this repo's own vendored `converge-wiring.mjs`. They ride this PR because `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push.

After this lands, this repo's parked items get `needs-human` dropped and `task:ready` added, and its agentic lane works.

input.title: The flip removed the `overrides` dispatch input, so Sheepdog's fleet-forcing apparatus refuses on every flipped member
input.body:
Found while wiring the remaining members for #916 — Sheepdog #213 was parked `needs-human` for a reason unrelated to the endpoint fault.

## What happens

The two scheduler stubs land at the **same path**, `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, but declare different interfaces:

- slot stub ([`stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml:28`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml#L28)) — `workflow_dispatch: inputs: overrides`
- queue stub ([`stubs/claudinite-tick.yml:27`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-tick.yml#L27)) — bare `workflow_dispatch`, no inputs

Sheepdog's fleet tasks dispatch that workflow **with** an `overrides` input carrying `FORCE_TASKS=…`. GitHub rejects a dispatch naming an input the workflow does not declare, so the moment a member flips, every such dispatch fails.

Live, from Sheepdog #213 at 06:57Z — 7 of the members it tried:

> unfired: missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary: **not-dispatchable** — the workflow exists but refused the dispatch — it is disabled (GitHub switches off cron on inactive repos), or too old to accept the `overrides` input

…and the same for ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, ShoutsAndWhispers, VascularColoring. The task then failed and escalated.

## Why this matters more than one task

`fleet-baseline` is the fleet's **force-a-member-to-converge lever** — the one this project's own working rules mandate using whenever a change to what members receive lands ("drive Sheepdog's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, report per member unasked"). It forces via `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` through exactly this input. So on a flipped member that lever is gone, and the mandated verification step silently cannot run.

That also makes the slot deletion (#801 Step 3's last item) more than a cleanup: deleting `FORCE_TASKS` removes the mechanism these tasks still call, rather than removing something already unused.

## The misdiagnosis is part of the bug

The message blames a **disabled workflow** or a **too-old stub** — both of which point at a platform setting or a stale member. The actual cause is the opposite: the member is *current*, and the new stub is the one that dropped the input. Anyone following that message goes looking at repo settings, which this project's own rules warn against ("propose a platform-settings change only as a conclusion, never as a diagnosis"). Whatever the fix, that string needs to name "the member runs the queue stub, which declares no inputs" as a distinct, detectable case — it is distinguishable, since the dispatch 422s with the unexpected-input error rather than a 403/404.

## Direction

In the queue, forcing is not a dispatch at all — it is **waking the standing item** (DESIGN §8: strip `task:blocked`, add `task:ready`, clear `Not-before`), an issue edit. So the fleet tasks should wake the member's standing item over the API instead of dispatching with overrides; Sheepdog already holds the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` that needs. `create-work-item.mjs`'s force path is the shape, applied cross-repo.

A dispatch is still needed to make the member's executor pick the woken item up promptly, but that one carries no inputs and works on both stubs.

Blocks the slot deletion in #801 Step 3, and blocks the mandated `fleet-baseline` verification for every flipped member in the meantime.

Owner-only steps, one checkbox per repo. Blocks the agentic half of #801 Step 3.

**Done 2026-08-16 12:35Z.** All ten adopted members have a routine, a token and a merged wiring PR; their parked agentic items are re-queued and draining.

## What was broken

`taskScheduler.endpoints` was declared in **exactly one repo in the fleet: this one.** Every member had none, so `resolveEndpoint` failed at the *declaration* before it ever looked for a token, and every agentic work item converged to `needs-human`:

> Could not start an agent session: this repo's config declares no invocation endpoint "default" (taskScheduler.endpoints)

Agentless tasks were unaffected and ran clean throughout.

### The stored prompt — identical for every routine

```
Read .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md — or engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md if that path does not exist — and follow it exactly.
```

The rule to land: letting go of an open item kills your claim."    - **Final:** "All repos have secrets, here are the URLs for the CCRs" — 10 routine URLs, to be wired across the fleet.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Work-item queue** (tasks-dispatch DESIGN): the GitHub issue *is* the durable object. Labels: `task:blocked`, `task:ready`, `task:urgent`, `task:executing`, `task:agent`, `needs-human`, `origin:schedule`, `outcome:done|delivered|obsolete`.
   - **Tick** (`engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs`): three deterministic jobs — instantiate standing items at anchors, ready blocked items, reclaim dead executor claims (executing leash 60m). Evaluates no preconditions.
   - **Executor** (`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs`): pull worker; pick → claim by verified lease → single precondition evaluation → work step → converge or hand off.
   - **Claim arbitration**: earliest claim comment by **comment id** (never timestamp), scoped to the current *episode* — the boundary is the last `EPISODE_MARKER` comment (F18).
   - **Vendored mount**: `.claudinite/shared/` replaced wholesale by `updates/engine-update.mjs`; vendor set computed by `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs`.
   - **Wiring converge** (`engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs`): stamps `required_secrets` + endpoint token names into workflows under a `# claudinite:secrets` marker. Cannot push `.github/workflows/`.
   - **CCR invocation** (`engine/scheduler/queue/invoke.mjs`): at-most-once, one call per item, never retried; `resolveEndpoint` reads `taskScheduler.endpoints`.
   - **Simulator** (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/sim.mjs`): discrete-event model; scenarios in `scenarios.test.mjs`; findings table F1–F24 in `SCENARIOS.md`.
   - Repo working rules: see-it-fail before fixing; anchored text edits to JSON (never re-serialize); `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`; merge via squash + `capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`; one Claude_Code_Remote call per intent.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs`** — the vendor-set computation; engine `.md` files are dropped as maintainer reference except an operational whitelist. **Changed** (merged as #907):
     ```js
     // `queue/instructions.md` is the whole behavior of a work-item session: the CCR
     // routine's stored prompt is one line pointing at it in the mount, so a member
     // missing it starts an agent hop with no instructions at all.
     const VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS = new Set([
       'engine/scheduler/executor.md',
       'engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md',
       'engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md',
     ]);
     ```

   - **`vendoring/compute-vendor-set.test.mjs`** — extended the real-canon-tree regression test and added a directory-wide guard:
     ```js
     assert.ok(files.includes('engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md'),
       'the live queue instructions.md must be in the vendor set — the routine\'s stored prompt points a queue session at it in the mount');
     ...
     test('regression: the REAL canon tree vendors the WHOLE queue engine, .md included', async () => {
       const onDisk = readdirSync(queueDir).filter((n) => !n.endsWith('.test.mjs'));
       for (const name of onDisk) {
         assert.ok(files.includes(`engine/scheduler/queue/${name}`), ...);
       }
     });
     ```

   - **`engine/scheduler/github.mjs`** — added the only sanctioned comment edit (merged as #925):
     ```js
     // The ONE sanctioned edit to a comment... an executor striking its OWN claim on
     // the way out (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6.2). Only a claim's author ever edits it,
     // so a claim can be withdrawn but never forged earlier...
     export const editComment = (gh, repo, commentId, body) =>
       gh(`/repos/${repo}/issues/comments/${commentId}`, { method: 'PATCH', body: { body } });
     ```

   - **`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs`** — F24 fix. Added `strikeClaim`, threaded `claim` through `converge`/`executeItem`/`handOff`, struck at roll and at the losing-claimant path:
     ```js
     async function strikeClaim(api, gh, repo, claim) {
       if (!claim || (claim.body ?? '').includes(EPISODE_MARKER)) return;
       await api.editComment(gh, repo, claim.id,
         `${claim.body}\n\n${EPISODE_MARKER}\nThis claim is spent — the executor released this item without closing it.`);
     }

     async function converge(api, gh, repo, number, from, to, claim, body) {
       await strikeClaim(api, gh, repo, claim);
       await api.comment(gh, repo, number, body);
       await api.swapLabel(gh, repo, number, from, to);
     }
     ```
     Losing-claimant path:
     ```js
     const mine = [...comments].sort((a, b) => a.id - b.id)
       .filter((c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(CLAIM_MARKER) && (c.body ?? '').includes(`executor \`${executorId}\``))
       .at(-1);
     if (!winner || winner.id !== mine?.id) {
       await strikeClaim(api, gh, repo, mine);
       log(`- #${candidate.number}: another executor holds this episode's earliest claim — moving on`);
       continue;
     }
     ```
     Roll path gained `await strikeClaim(api, gh, repo, claim);` before the body PATCH.
     The unchanged defect site, `claimWinner` (lines 92–99), is the diagnosis anchor:
     ```js
     const boundary = sorted.filter((c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(EPISODE_MARKER)).at(-1);
     const claims = sorted.filter((c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(CLAIM_MARKER))
       .filter((c) => !boundary || c.id > boundary.id);
     return claims[0] ?? null;
     ```

     // F18/F24: the episode boundary is an ARTIFACT on the item, not a property of
     // the label transition... A human re-queue deliberately does NOT advance it.
     function endEpisode(it) { it.claimEpoch = seq++; }
     ```

   - **`docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md`** — added the S39/F24 narrative in the S32 block and the `F24` row to the findings table.

       "default": {

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

{"number":929,"title":"The flip removed the `overrides` dispatch input, so Sheepdog's fleet-forcing apparatus refuses on every flipped member","body":"Found while wiring the remaining members for #916 — Sheepdog #213 was parked `needs-human` for a reason unrelated to the endpoint fault.

## What happens

The two scheduler stubs land at the **same path**, `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, but declare different interfaces:

- slot stub ([`stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml:28`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml#L28)) — `workflow_dispatch: inputs: overrides`
- queue stub ([`stubs/claudinite-tick.yml:27`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-tick.yml#L27)) — bare `workflow_dispatch`, no inputs

Sheepdog's fleet tasks dispatch that workflow **with** an `overrides` input carrying `FORCE_TASKS=…`. GitHub rejects a dispatch naming an input the workflow does not declare, so the moment a member flips, every such dispatch fails.

Live, from Sheepdog #213 at 06:57Z — 7 of the members it tried:

> unfired: missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary: **not-dispatchable** — the workflow exists but refused the dispatch — it is disabled (GitHub switches off cron on inactive repos), or too old to accept the `overrides` input

…and the same for ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, ShoutsAndWhispers, VascularColoring. The task then failed and escalated.

## Why this matters more than one task

`fleet-baseline` is the fleet's **force-a-member-to-converge lever** — the one this project's own working rules mandate using whenever a change to what members receive lands ("drive Sheepdog's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, report per member unasked"). It forces via `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` through exactly this input. So on a flipped member that lever is gone, and the mandated verification step silently cannot run.

That also makes the slot deletion (#801 Step 3's last item) more than a cleanup: deleting `FORCE_TASKS` removes the mechanism these tasks still call, rather than removing something already unused.

## The misdiagnosis is part of the bug

The message blames a **disabled workflow** or a **too-old stub** — both of which point at a platform setting or a stale member. The actual cause is the opposite: the member is *current*, and the new stub is the one that dropped the input. Anyone following that message goes looking at repo settings, which this project's own rules warn against ("propose a platform-settings change only as a conclusion, never as a diagnosis"). Whatever the fix, that string needs to name "the member runs the queue stub, which declares no inputs" as a distinct, detectable case — it is distinguishable, since the dispatch 422s with the unexpected-input error rather than a 403/404.

## Direction

In the queue, forcing is not a dispatch at all — it is **waking the standing item** (DESIGN §8: strip `task:blocked`, add `task:ready`, clear `Not-before`), an issue edit. So the fleet tasks should wake the member's standing item over the API instead of dispatching with overrides; Sheepdog already holds the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` that needs. `create-work-item.mjs`'s force path is the shape, applied cross-repo.

A dispatch is still needed to make the member's executor pick the woken item up promptly, but that one carries no inputs and works on both stubs.

Blocks the slot deletion in #801 Step 3, and blocks the mandated `fleet-baseline` verification for every flipped member in the meantime.

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [x] The first member flipped, wired and observed end to end — agentless and agentic
- [ ] All members flipped and observed; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] Step 4: the fielded engine matches DESIGN §15.14–24 — #883 closed
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

150	  // The tracked declaration file is THE membership signal — the one file every
151	  // member carries whatever its mount shape (the engine can't run without it,
152	  // and baselining backfills it nightly), and the only shape the planner can
153	  // plan for at all (activePacks is read from it). A mount marker WITHOUT a
154	  // declaration is a half-adoption that must classify as uncovered — the roster
155	  // then opens an adoption issue and it heals loudly, instead of rotting as a
156	  // "covered" repo no task ever runs on. (vendoring/DESIGN.md)
157	  return fileExists(gh, fullName, '.claudinite-checks.json');
158	}
159	
160	// --- firing a member's own scheduler -------------------------------------------
161	
162	// The member-side workflow every fan-out fires, and the shape of the firing. Two of
163	// this pack's tasks press this button — fleet-baseline (each member baselines itself)
164	// and fleet-add-missing-packs (each member adopts the packs its work-list issue names)
165	// — so the primitive lives here on the shared floor rather than in either task. The
166	// fan-out model is the point (#749): the enforcer DISPATCHES, the member EXECUTES —
167	// every agentic step happens inside the member, under its own scheduler, executor and
168	// grant, so no agent anywhere needs cross-repo access. The one credential is the PAT,
169	// and the one scope beyond the read-only sweeps' is Actions WRITE (a workflow_dispatch
170	// POST is an Actions write).
171	export const SCHEDULER = 'claudinite-scheduler.yml';
172	
173	// Fire one member's scheduler with a FORCE_TASKS override, ONE task id per fire —
174	// the override bag splits pairs on commas (engine parseOverrides), so a
175	// comma-separated id list would not survive the trip, and no fan-out here wants more
176	// than one task anyway. `ref` is the member's DEFAULT branch (read from the
177	// enumeration, never assumed to be `main`): workflow_dispatch resolves the workflow
178	// file on the ref it is given, and a repo whose trunk is `master` would otherwise 404
179	// as if it carried no scheduler at all. A forced run evaluates ONLY the named task
180	// (engine/scheduler/run.mjs, #749) — never the member's coincident backlog.
181	export async function fireScheduler(gh, fullName, ref, taskId) {
182	  const { status } = await gh(`/repos/${fullName}/actions/workflows/${SCHEDULER}/dispatches`, {
183	    method: 'POST',
184	    body: { ref, inputs: { overrides: `FORCE_TASKS=${taskId}` } },
185	  });
186	  return classifyDispatch(status);
187	}
188	
189	// What the dispatch POST's status means. Every branch is a DIFFERENT thing for the
190	// reader to do, which is why callers report a state per repo instead of a count of
191	// failures: a 404 is a repo to adopt, a 403 is a token to re-scope, a 422 is a
192	// workflow GitHub has switched off. Kept free of I/O so the whole table is testable.
193	export function classifyDispatch(status) {
194	  switch (status) {
195	    case 204:
196	      return { state: 'fired', detail: 'queued on its own scheduler' };
197	    case 404:
198	      // The workflow is missing, the repo has Actions disabled, or the PAT cannot see
199	      // the repo at all — indistinguishable from here, and all three mean "nothing was
200	      // queued".
201	      return { state: 'no-scheduler', detail: `no ${SCHEDULER} on the default branch, or Actions is disabled — nothing there can run its own tasks` };
202	    case 403:
203	      return { state: 'no-permission', detail: 'the PAT lacks Actions: write on this repo — dispatching a workflow is an Actions write, a scope the read-only sweeps never needed' };
204	    case 422:
205	      // GitHub disables a repo's scheduled workflows after 60 days of inactivity, and a
206	      // disabled workflow refuses dispatch; a scheduler stub too old to carry the
207	      // `overrides` input lands here too.
208	      return { state: 'not-dispatchable', detail: 'the workflow exists but refused the dispatch — it is disabled (GitHub switches off cron on inactive repos), or too old to accept the `overrides` input' };
209	    default:
210	      return { state: 'error', detail: `dispatch returned ${status}` };
211	  }

- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

--- §11 ---
## 11. Recovery — what the janitor keeps, what dies

| failure | today | proposed |
|---|---|---|
| scheduler/tick miss or late fire | run-ledger catch-up math | same property from the occurrence guard (§5) — the next tick instantiates the most recent occurrence only |
| double tick | concurrency group + slot-title search | concurrency group + occurrence-guard search (same window, same answer) |
| lost label event | janitor re-arm (remove/re-add), 20-min grace, bounded by stale escalation | **retired** — executors poll on the tick's cron; events are latency sugar, never the only delivery |
| duplicate events / racing executors | claim lease on one implicit executor | same lease, N executors — the loser picks a different item |
| executor died mid-claim | — (executor was a session; janitor reclaimed via `agent-running`) | **the tick** (owner, 2026-08-13): `task:executing` with no activity past ~1h → strip to `task:ready` with a comment, so a dead executor's item is back in the queue within ~2h rather than ~25h. An executor iteration is minutes, not hours, and a lease checked once a day is not a short lease |
| executor run died with items still queued | n/a (one implicit executor; the next slot was a day away) | **the failure-continuation job** (owner, 2026-08-15): `needs: execute`, `if: failure() \|\| cancelled()` re-dispatches on a fresh runner, so the *queue* resumes in ~a minute while the dead run's own item waits for the leash; the tick drain is the backstop when the whole workflow run is lost (§10, S36) |
| agent session died mid-run | janitor: stale `agent-running` → `needs-human` after ~3h | same, on `task:agent` (a hand-off comment names the session, so the janitor can say *which* session died) |
| CCR invocation lost | undetectable (label event fired into the void); surfaced only by re-arm/stale | **synchronous**: a refused call converges `needs-human` with the error at once; an unanswered call leaves the item with the agent and the agent leash settles it — one call per item, never retried (§6.6) |
| item never picked up | stale dispatch escalation, period parsed from the slot id's leading char | same escalation, period read from the task's declared `frequency` at HEAD (or a default for ad-hoc items) — no title parsing; the stale item converges `needs-human`, out of the queue |
| dependency never resolves | n/a | **the stale-ready rule cannot see it** — a blocked item is never ready (F14, caught by the simulator against S18's claim). The janitor gains a third rule: a blocked item whose blockers have not resolved for ~2 days gets an escalation *comment* — labels untouched, so the item still proceeds by itself the moment its blockers resolve; a human who decides it is dead closes it by hand |

its grace window delete, and the **executing-leash reclaim moves to the tick**
— a deterministic label rule, serialized and hourly, which is exactly the
tick's kind of work. This amends the 2026-08-06 "all recovery lives in the
janitor" split, deliberately: the split's purpose was that recovery happen
*once, in one place, in code* rather than in every triggered session, and a
rule that runs once per tick satisfies that as fully as one that runs once per
day. What stays with the janitor is everything needing judgment or a longer
horizon — four rules and a review: the dead *agent* claim (`task:agent`

died), the stale-ready escalation (unpicked past ~2 periods →

nor `needs-human` — a torn label swap's leavings, §6.2 → `needs-human`),
and the health review, which gains the queue (ready-item age, blocked-item
depth, outcome mix) as its subject and can now compute all of it from
issues.

the first **reframed by the work-as-work review (2026-08-15)**:

  heartbeat is what buys that (F17, reframed).** As first written, F17 made

  inflates it to the heaviest task in the fleet: one legitimate three-hour
  task and a dead executor on a two-minute task also waits three hours to
  reclaim. Instead the executor **comments a heartbeat on the item every ~15

  long it works (S31c), a dead one stops heartbeating and is reclaimed within

  the wiring-time conformance check shrinks to the one relation the heartbeat

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/sha/7e50beda8877559822c35f375ae51b93b3588207/contents/.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml] # Claudinite work-item queue — the generator tick and its drain (tasks-dispatch
# DESIGN §5, §10). This is the repo's ONLY cron, and it replaces the slot
# scheduler's content at the same path when `taskScheduler.dispatch` is `"queue"`
# — same file, same hashed minute, different mechanism, so the one-cron rule and
# every reader that knows this workflow by name keep holding.
#
# A thin shim: all logic lives in the vendored engine, so this file changes
# rarely. The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap and the wiring converge
# rewrite it to this repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`.
#
# TWO JOBS, IN ORDER. The tick is pure label mechanics over the issue list —
# instantiate each task's standing item at its anchor, ready what is due, reclaim
# dead executor claims — and evaluates no precondition and collects no signal. The
# drain is an ordinary executor run: it picks up what the tick just created, which
# is what keeps the common case's latency at zero even with no `labeled` event
# delivered. Lost events are therefore never the only delivery — they are latency
# sugar, which is what retires the re-arm.
#
# `workflow_dispatch` is not a convenience: it is the never-wait-for-the-cron
# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '26 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# One tick at a time, always. The tick's duplicate-standing-item self-heal is
# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,
# which is safe precisely because two ticks never run at once.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-tick
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; a task's prework pushes its delivery branch
  issues: write          # create / label / comment / close work items — the queue itself
  pull-requests: write   # a task's prework opens its PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (creating a workflow_dispatch event needs write; `read` silently 403s the POST)

jobs:
  tick:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs

  # The post-tick drain. `timeout-minutes` MUST stay ≤ the engine's executing
  # leash (60m): a hung runner has to be killed by the platform before its claim
  # is reaped and the item re-picked, or a zombie's prework runs beside its
  # replacement's.
  drain:
    needs: tick
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Drain the queue
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # The wiring converge stamps every declared required_secret, and every
          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
          # claudinite:secrets
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue. Converges to ONE open
  # issue by a fixed title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a
  # first-run failure may precede any label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: [tick, drain]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite tick/drain run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

# scheduler's content at the same path when `taskScheduler.dispatch` is `"queue"`

#

+// its standing item, and this is that same lever reached from OUTSIDE the repo: the
+// fleet enforcer dispatches this workflow with the task ids it wants run now, and
+// the member wakes its own items with its own token. The enforcer therefore needs
+// no issue access anywhere — the fan-out model the sheepdog pack is built on, where
+// the enforcer dispatches and the member executes.
+// An id is `pack/task` or a bare `task` resolved against this repo's own discovered
+// tasks, so a caller spanning many members never has to know any one member's pack
+// layout. Every id that matches nothing comes back in `unmatched`: a force whose
+// report counts only what it woke reads as coverage it did not have.
+// An item already in flight (`task:ready`, `task:executing`, `task:agent`) is left
+// alone and reported as `already`, never re-woken — an episode boundary dropped on
+// a live claim is exactly the livelock F18 describes.
+export function planWake(spec, tasks = [], items = []) {
+  const ids = String(spec ?? '').split(/[\s,]+/).map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
+  const wake = []; const already = []; const unmatched = [];
+  for (const id of ids) {
+    const [a, b] = id.includes('/') ? id.split('/') : [null, id];
+    const owners = tasks.filter((t) => t.id === b && (a === null || t.pack === a));
+    if (owners.length !== 1) {
+      unmatched.push({ id, why: owners.length ? `${owners.length} declared packs own a "${b}" task — name it as pack/task` : 'no declared pack owns a task by that name' });
+      continue;
+    const { pack, id: task } = owners[0];
+    const item = items.find((i) => {
+      if (i.state !== 'open') return false;
+      const parsed = parseWorkItemTitle(i.title);
+      return parsed && parsed.pack === pack && parsed.task === task;
+    if (!item) { unmatched.push({ id, why: `no open standing item for ${pack}/${task}` }); continue; }
+    if (IN_FLIGHT.some((l) => hasLabel(item, l))) { already.push({ id, issue: item.number }); continue; }
+    wake.push({ id: `${pack}/${task}`, issue: item.number });
+  return { wake, already, unmatched };
