# TWO JOBS, IN ORDER. The tick is pure label mechanics over the issue list —
# instantiate each task's standing item at its anchor, ready what is due, reclaim
# dead executor claims — and evaluates no precondition and collects no signal. The
# drain is an ordinary executor run: it picks up what the tick just created, which
# is what keeps the common case's latency at zero even with no `labeled` event
# delivered. Lost events are therefore never the only delivery — they are latency
# sugar, which is what retires the re-arm.
#
# `workflow_dispatch` is not a convenience: it is the never-wait-for-the-cron
# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on. Its one
# input is how that lever reaches ACROSS repos: the fleet enforcer dispatches
# this workflow naming the tasks to run now, and this member wakes its own
# standing items with its own token (DESIGN §8). The alternative — the enforcer
# editing every member's issues directly — would widen the fleet PAT to issue
# writes on every repository, for a job the member can do for itself.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '44 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wake:
        description: 'Task ids to run now (`pack/task` or a bare task name, space-separated) — wakes each one’s standing item regardless of its anchor'
        required: false
        type: string

# One tick at a time, always. The tick's duplicate-standing-item self-heal is
# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,
# which is safe precisely because two ticks never run at once.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-tick
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; a task's prework pushes its delivery branch
  issues: write          # create / label / comment / close work items — the queue itself
  pull-requests: write   # a task's prework opens its PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (creating a workflow_dispatch event needs write; `read` silently 403s the POST)

jobs:
  tick:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs

  # The post-tick drain. `timeout-minutes` MUST stay ≤ the engine's executing
  # leash (60m): a hung runner has to be killed by the platform before its claim
  # is reaped and the item re-picked, or a zombie's prework runs beside its
  # replacement's.
  drain:
    needs: tick
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Drain the queue
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # On a member this block is stamped by the wiring converge (the
          # `# claudinite:secrets` marker in the stub); the canon has no converge,
          # so its own list is written here, by hand, in the same commit.
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
          CCR_FLEET_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_FLEET_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
        run: node engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue. Converges to ONE open
  # issue by a fixed title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a
  # first-run failure may precede any label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: [tick, drain]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite tick/drain run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

input.head: claude/dispatcher-executor-801-7x3ak6
input.title: Restore fleet forcing under the queue: a `wake` input the member acts on
input.body:
Fixes #929, fixes #921. Refs #801 (Step 3).

## The problem

Both scheduler stubs land at `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, but they declare **different dispatch interfaces** — the slot stub took an `overrides` input, the queue stub took none. Sheepdog's two fan-out tasks still dispatched with `overrides=FORCE_TASKS=…`, and GitHub 422s a dispatch naming an input the workflow does not declare.

So every fleet-wide force has refused since the flip. Live, from Sheepdog #213 at 06:57Z, 7 members reported `not-dispatchable`. That takes out **`fleet-baseline`** — the fleet's force-a-member-to-converge lever, and the one this project's rules mandate driving whenever a change to what members receive lands.

## The fix, and why not the direction #929 proposed

#929 proposed the enforcer wake each member's standing item over the API. That works, but it needs **issue write on every repository** in the fleet PAT — a wider standing credential, which this project's rules treat as a last resort.

Instead the lever stays a dispatch, and the **member does its own edit**: the workflow declares a `wake` input, and the member's own tick wakes its own standing items with its own token. The fleet PAT stays at Actions write, and it matches the fan-out model the sheepdog pack is already built on — the enforcer dispatches, the member executes.

`planWake` is a pure planner beside `planTick`:

- resolves a bare task id against **the repo's own declared packs**, so a cross-fleet caller never needs to know any one member's pack layout
- refuses an ambiguous id rather than guessing which pack meant it
- leaves an **in-flight** item alone (`task:ready` / `task:executing` / `task:agent`) — an episode boundary dropped on a live claim is exactly F18's livelock
- reports every id that matched nothing, and **fails the run**: a force that woke nothing is a failed force, and a green run saying so in a log line is how it goes unnoticed by the lever that pressed it

The wake runs *after* the tick's ops, so an item this run just instantiated is wakeable in the same run — a force never has to be pressed twice.

## The misdiagnosis was half the bug

The 422 message blamed a disabled workflow or a stale member, sending a reader to **repo settings** when the member was current and the new stub was the one that dropped the input. It now names both causes and says the stale-mount case heals on the member's next converge.

## Guards

Both were reproduced against the real defect before the fix:

- **the input `fleet-api` sends must be one the stub declares** — checked against the stub *and* canon's own copy. Reverting the stub to a bare `workflow_dispatch` reproduces #929 exactly and fails this test. This is the guard that did not exist: the two spellings are the protocol and they live in different trees.
- **the tick must resolve the exact id `fleet-baseline` dispatches.**

The `planWake` unit tests were mutation-checked — dropping the in-flight guard or the unmatched reporting each fails a test.

## Also folded in (#921)

DESIGN §8's force recipe omitted `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on that label alone — so the documented recipe produced an item no executor could ever pick, and the run logged `nothing ready to pick up`, indistinguishable from a healthy idle run.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 1893 pass, 0 fail.

Landing this does not by itself restore the lever on fielded members: their workflow file predates the input, so a `wake` dispatch 422s until each converges. That is the transitional case the new 422 message names, and it self-heals hourly; I'll wake `core/update` by hand across the fleet after merge to close it in one pass rather than waiting.

content.text:
Meanwhile, your questions.

**Is the Sheepdog problem a migration thing or a real design issue?**

Migration. The queue design deliberately replaced "forcing = dispatch with `FORCE_TASKS`" with "forcing = wake the standing item." That change was made in the engine, but the forcing protocol's only *cross-repo* caller lives in `packs/sheepdog/` — and nobody ported it. The two stubs land at the same path with different dispatch interfaces, so every flipped member started rejecting the old call shape. The queue design itself is fine; what the migration plan missed is that a protocol has callers outside the module that defines it.

**Would the cleanup solve it?** No — the cleanup would have *deepened* it. Deleting the slot machinery removes `FORCE_TASKS`, which is precisely what Sheepdog still calls. So this was never a blocker sitting in front of the cleanup; **it is part of the cleanup** — `fireScheduler` is a slot-era call site, and retiring the slot protocol means porting it. That's why I did it first.

One thing I changed from what #929 proposed. That issue said the enforcer should wake each member's standing item over the API. That works, but it needs **issue write on every repository** in the fleet PAT. Your standing rule treats a wider credential as a last resort, so I took the route that needs no new grant: the workflow declares a `wake` input, and the member's own tick does its own edit with its own token. Same lever, credential unchanged, and it matches the fan-out model Sheepdog is already built on.

The guard that was missing is now there: the input name Sheepdog sends and the input the stub declares are the protocol, they live in different trees, and nothing checked they agreed. Reverting the stub reproduces #929 and fails the test.

content.text:
CI green on [#936](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/936) — 1,893 tests, conformance clean.

I stopped there rather than continuing into the deletion itself, because the deletion is genuinely gated on this merging: it removes `FORCE_TASKS`, which is what #936 replaces. Landing them together would mean deleting the old lever in the same commit that introduces the new one, with no green fleet in between.

**What the deletion actually involves**, now that I've scoped it: ~1,076 engine lines (`run.mjs`, `slots.mjs`, `run-record.mjs`, the slot stub) plus ~1,900 lines of slot-only tests. But it isn't an `rm` — the queue still reaches into the slot modules for three things: `FREQUENCIES` and `mostRecentSlot` (via `anchors.mjs` and `task-contract.mjs`) and `buildSignalContext` (via `queue/signals.mjs`). Those need extracting to their own homes first, or the deletion takes the queue down with it. That's the real work; the rest is mechanical.

**What else is open.** On #801's path: the slot deletion, then the fan-out/fan-in migration item (the migration reporting itself through its own mechanism), then Step 4 — [#883](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/883)'s seven work-as-work behaviors, with [#892](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/892) carrying the durable-record box, [#924](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/924) riding the heartbeat, and [#877](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/877) last so the rename doesn't churn files mid-migration.

Separately, live traffic has kept surfacing things: [#926](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/926) (the declarative vocabulary never reached a member's local pack), [#920](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/920) (`sharedMount`'s regex is mount-only, so the signal is dead in canon itself).

**One live observation worth your attention.** TLDR has three items sitting in `task:agent` for ~9 hours — sessions that started, did the work (its tidy trackers were updated), and never converged the item. Root cause: TLDR's mount still lacks `queue/instructions.md`, so those sessions got no instructions at all. #907 fixed that in canon, but TLDR can't receive it until its `core/update` item reaches its 04:00Z anchor — and `fleet-baseline`, the lever that would collapse that wait, is the very thing #936 restores. The janitor's 3h agent leash will park them `needs-human` at its next run, so nothing is lost, but they'll be parked despite having succeeded — which is [#892](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/892) showing up at fleet scale rather than on one repo.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#936](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/936) is green and awaiting your merge — it closes #929 and #921. It changes direction from what #929 proposed (member-side wake via a dispatch input, rather than the enforcer editing issues cross-fleet) specifically to avoid widening `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` to issue-write on every repo; worth a look at that call. The slot deletion is scoped and ready to start the moment #936 lands — it needs `FREQUENCIES`, `mostRecentSlot` and `buildSignalContext` extracted out of the slot modules first, since the queue still imports them. Not yet done: waking `core/update` across the fleet to deliver #907/#925 (I'll do that post-merge, per the PR), and #892, which the TLDR items above make more urgent than its `quick-win` label suggests.

1	---
2	name: merge-to-main
3	description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
4	---
5	
6	
7	The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.
8	
9	**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.
10	
11	## Recipe (~4 calls)
12	
13	1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
14	2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
15	3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
16	4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
17	5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
18	
19	The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.
20	
21	## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)
22	
23	Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
24	`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.
25	
26	## Don't
27	
28	- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
29

description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
